items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 614-619 (book Theorem 10.1.14, Diaconescu theorem): the axiom of choice implies the law of excluded middle. The statement is a global implication between principles and gives no construction, and the proof (source lines 621-646) has to build the whole argument around one mere proposition A: the two-point map into the suspension of A has to be shown surjective, which needs a fibre over each pole and the fact that truncated fibres are mere propositions; choice then supplies a section merely, whose existence is used together with decidable equality of the booleans to produce a disjunction; and that disjunction has to be transported along the injectivity of the section and the identification of the equality of the two poles with A. Which form of choice is used, why the suspension of a proposition is the right type, and where decidability enters are all invisible in the statement.
